newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to send food to rebel-held areas.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to send food to rebel-held areas.

text.p: Sri Lanka will start sending much-needed food supplies to the northern rebel-held Wanni region at the weekend, where hundreds of people are said to have been displaced by the latest military offensive.

"Twelve lorries will be sent to the other side tomorrow. Another 40 lorries will be arranged on Sunday," a senior government official told Reuters in northern Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.

Kandiah Ganesh, government agent for Vavuniya, said food was short in some areas of the Wanni and immediate supplies were needed. He said the Defence Ministry had approved a route through western Mannar town to northern Kilinochchi and northeastern Mullaitivu districts, where the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels are fighting government troops.

Aid workers have said that food stocks in the Wanni were strained by additional numbers joining the list of displaced and with government supplies grinding to a halt after the latest offensive began earlier this month.
Some 20,000 troops launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru" or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.

The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, have accused Colombo of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their property under the pretext of opening a supply route.
They said earlier this week the government had launched a "food siege" and that the refugee crisis was spiralling out of control.
Ganesh said the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) had agreed to escort the food convoy to the Wanni, but was waiting for government permission.
The Defence Ministry said earlier this week that most of the Wanni except Kilinochchi district had sufficient food stocks for the next few weeks.
It said several thousand tonnes of wheat flour, rice, sugar and milk powder had been sent to the Wanni since October last year.
